label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. Despite advanced educational attainment, heavy digital engagement does not appear to buffer against psychological difficulties, and may coincide with social isolation and mental health challenges.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating perceived social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting persistent low mood and functional impact
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced of the three distress indicators
Extensive daily digital engagement exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety forming a compounded distress pattern
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting significant emotional burden across multiple mental health dimensions

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted and emotionally stable. They spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) on activities captured in the study, suggesting balanced engagement rather than excessive or minimal use.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77)
Engages in moderate daily usage of 1–3 hours, suggesting balanced habits
Belongs to a relatively well-represented group (n = 150) indicating a common, stable profile

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ~1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Below-average depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 mean ~0.86) suggesting subclinical mood levels
Below-average anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7 mean ~0.91) indicating minimal anxious distress
Relatively limited daily screen/media engagement (1–3 hours), possibly reflecting structured routines
Disconnect between social isolation feelings and affective symptom burden, suggesting compensatory coping
tone: Quietly isolated yet emotionally composed; reflective and self-sufficient rather than distressed
